raw_case_text:
A 45-year-old female with type II diabetes presented with a 5-month history of severe back pain. She was a homemaker who kept pigeons as pets. Her laboratory investigations revealed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 38 mm/1st h and a C-reactive protein (CRP) of 18 mg/l. The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated T4 osteomyelitis with relatively well-preserved intervertebral disc spaces [Figure 1]. Although fine-needle aspiration cytology was inconclusive, the patient was presumptively placed on antitubercular drugs. One month later, she became fully paraplegic. At that point, the MRI demonstrated osteolytic lesions of the T4 vertebral body with cord compression, accompanied by bilateral paraspinal soft tissue masses extending to the T5-T6 level; there was, however, no disc space involvement [Figure 2]. She underwent a biopsy of the T4 vertebral body, accompanied by transfacet T4 decompression, and posterior T2- T6 pedicle screw instrumentation [Figure 3].
The culture and histopathological examinations revealed a cryptococcal fungal infection that was sensitive to amphotericin B; this was administered intravenously (150 mg/day) for the next 3 months [Figure 4]. However, the patient developed an abscess at the surgical site 2 weeks later, which required drainage. Three weeks postoperatively, she also developed the sudden loss of vision bilaterally; the ophthalmological examination revealed bilateral retinal fungal deposits and endophthalmitis. One eye's vision recovered after intravitreal voriconazole, but she lost vision in the other eye despite vitrectomy. The amphotericin B antibiotic regimen was then supplemented with flucytosine (i.e., 500 mg thrice a day) until the 3rd postoperative month.
Three months following the spinal surgery, she regained 4/5 function in both lower extremities. Although the MRI still showed some prevertebral collection compared with the preoperative MRI, there was resolution of the T4 cord compression [Figure 5]. Eight months postoperatively, the patient could walk with a cane but had residual unilateral loss of vision (perception of light only). Furthermore, the ESR and CRP levels both normalized. In addition, the MRI now showed complete resolution of the prevertebral abscess and the previously abnormal signal within the T3-T5 vertebral bodies [Figure 6]. After 3 postoperative months passed, intravenous amphotericin B was stopped, but she was kept on oral fluconazole 400 mg once a day, and flucytosine 500 mg thrice a day for 5 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 45-year-old female homemaker with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 5-month history of severe back pain that progressed 1 month later to complete paraplegia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with 5 months of severe thoracic back pain and was initially placed on empirical anti-tubercular therapy after an inconclusive fine-needle aspiration of a T4 vertebral lesion. One month later, she progressed to complete paraplegia. She kept pet pigeons at home.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; homemaker who kept pet pigeons.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe back pain, progressive lower extremity paralysis, and subsequent postoperative bilateral sudden visual loss.

objective.physical_examination: Progressed to complete paraplegia (0/5 lower extremity motor power) 1 month after initial presentation; 3 weeks postoperatively, developed sudden bilateral vision loss with bilateral retinal fungal deposits and endophthalmitis on ophthalmological examination.
objective.routine_investigations: ESR 38 mm/1st hour and CRP 18 mg/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial thoracic spine MRI showed T4 osteomyelitis with preserved intervertebral discs; repeat MRI at onset of paraplegia demonstrated osteolytic destruction of the T4 vertebral body with spinal cord compression and bilateral paraspinal soft tissue masses extending to T5-T6, sparing the disc spaces. Intraoperative T4 vertebral biopsy histopathology and fungal culture (obtained during transfacet T4 decompression and T2-T6 posterior pedicle screw instrumentation) confirmed amphotericin B-sensitive Cryptococcus infection.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of T4 vertebral cryptococcal osteomyelitis (spondylitis) with epidural/paraspinal abscess and cord compression complicated postoperatively by bilateral endogenous cryptococcal endophthalmitis in a diabetic patient with pet pigeon exposure, confirmed by T4 vertebral biopsy histopathology and fungal culture. Treated with T4 transfacet decompression and T2-T6 pedicle screw fixation, surgical wound abscess drainage at week 2, intravitreal voriconazole and pars plana vitrectomy at week 3, 3 months of IV amphotericin B (150 mg/day) plus oral flucytosine (500 mg three times daily), and 5 subsequent months of oral fluconazole (400 mg/day) plus flucytosine (500 mg three times daily). At 8 months postoperatively, ESR/CRP and spinal MRI normalized and she ambulated with a cane (4/5 lower limb strength), with visual recovery in one eye and residual light-perception-only vision in the vitrectomized eye.
